data.text/markdown:
Late-delivery model (interactive)

Question. When a customer places an order, can we tell which orders are most likely to arrive after the delivery date they were promised? This is the interactive version of 02_late_delivery_model.ipynb. The logic is the same tested code in src/ml/; here you can change the controls and watch the charts respond. The written summary is docs/ml/MODEL_CARD.md. To run it: build the warehouse first (uv run python src/transformation/build_warehouse.py), then uv run marimo edit notebooks/marimo/02_late_delivery_model.py (or marimo run for the app view). What to expect. A moderate ranker, not a crystal ball: flagging the riskiest 10% of orders catches late deliveries about 2.8 times better than chance on average.
96,282 delivered orders, 8.1% arrived late; 16 numeric + 3 categorical features.

1. The data

The label is is_late: the order arrived after the estimated delivery date shown at checkout. About 8% of delivered orders are late, but that rate swings a lot from month to month, which is the main difficulty.

data.text/html: <div style='display: flex;flex: 1;flex-direction: column;justify-content: flex-start;align-items: normal;flex-wrap: nowrap;gap: 0.5rem'><marimo-mime-renderer data-mime='"application/vnd.marimo+mimebundle"' data-data='"{\"image/png\": \"data:image/png;base64,\", \"__metadata__\": {\"image/png\": {\"width\": 764, \"height\": 372}}}"'></marimo-mime-renderer><span class="markdown prose dark:prose-invert contents"><span class="paragraph">The three groups mostly move together, driven by the month. <strong>In August 2018 they split apart: orders promised in under 20 days are late about 14% of the time, while the 30+ day promises are almost never late.</strong> Which promise length is "risky" is not constant over time; this is why the model struggles in the last test month.</span></span></div>

data.text/markdown:
2. How the model is tested

Orders are tested in time order, never shuffled: for each test month the model trains only on orders whose delivery was already known before that month began, then scores that month's orders. The blue bar is what the model could learn from; the orange bar is the month it is scored on.

3. Training and scoring

One logistic regression per test month, on 19 features known at purchase (the promised window, basket size and weight, customer and seller state, distance, weekday and hour, payment, and the seller's earlier late rate). Nothing known only after delivery is used (LEAKAGE_ANALYSIS.md). This cell takes about 15 seconds.

data.text/html: base_rate is what random guessing achieves; pr_auc is how well the ranking concentrates late orders at the top; precision_at_top and recall_at_top describe the riskiest 10% of orders.

<div style='display: flex;flex: 1;flex-direction: column;justify-content: flex-start;align-items: normal;flex-wrap: nowrap;gap: 0.5rem'><marimo-mime-renderer data-mime='"application/vnd.marimo+mimebundle"' data-data='"{\"image/png\": \"data:image/png;base64,\", \"__metadata__\": {\"image/png\": {\"width\": 764, \"height\": 387}}}"'></marimo-mime-renderer><span class="markdown prose dark:prose-invert contents"><span class="paragraph">Flagging the riskiest <strong>10%</strong> finds late deliveries <strong>2.8x</strong> more often than chance on average, and catches <strong>28%</strong> of all late orders. Slide the control: flagging more orders catches more of the late ones but dilutes the precision. At 10% the lift is 2.4 to 3.9 times in five months and only 1.2 times in August 2018.</span></span></div>

data.text/markdown:
Left: inside a month the ranking is sensible (higher predicted risk, higher actual rate), though the riskiest group is over-predicted. Right: the level is wrong by month; the model predicted about 7% in March 2018 when the real rate was 21%. The late rate swings in a way the past does not predict (recalibrating on recent data made things worse, see RECALIBRATION_AND_WINDOW.md). So: use the model by rank, flagging a share of orders, not by quoting probabilities.

4. What does the model rely on?

Permutation importance: shuffle one group of related columns in a test month and see how much ranking quality (PR-AUC) drops. This takes about a minute, so it runs only when you press the button.

data.text/markdown: Press the button above to compute.

A longer promise (promised_days) is the strongest numeric effect and lowers the risk. Some destination states carry a high risk (Alagoas, Rio de Janeiro) and others a low one (Paraná, Minas Gerais, São Paulo). State and payment-type columns are one-hot with no reference category, so compare states with states, not with payment types.

5. What I tried that did not help

The plain model ("v1") was never beaten. Pick the measure to compare:
set adds
v1 the features above (the reference)
v2 late-rate history for the route and the product category
v3 v2 plus the system-wide late rate over the previous 28 days
v5 v1 plus delivery-time slack (promised days minus how long deliveries on the route have been taking)

data.text/markdown:
6. Why August 2018 breaks the model

For each month, how well does a single feature rank that month's orders on its own? An AUC of 0.5 means no skill; below 0.5 means the feature points the wrong way. Choose the features to compare:

The model had learned that a long promise on a long route is safe; in August the rule no longer held.</span></span></div>

data.text/markdown:
Takeaways

  • The model ranks orders moderately well. Flagging the riskiest 10% finds late deliveries about 2.8 times better than chance on average (1.2 times in the worst month).
  • Use it by rank, not by probability. The monthly late rate cannot be predicted from the past, so the level of its probabilities is unreliable.
  • It rests on the route and the promise. Everything else adds little.
  • It is fragile to policy change. A sharp change in how delivery dates are promised breaks it; a monitor on the distribution of promised days is worth having.
  • More features did not help, and the notebook shows the evidence.
Limits. Six test months, one market, data ending in 2018, no tuning. Details are in MODEL_CARD.md.
